title: Publish preview.decide as a human-only kind with its refusal codes
description:

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: the vocabulary half only - `preview.decide` published as an operator-only command kind with its full roster backfill and its four stable refusal codes. It runs no process, captures no screenshot and renders nothing. Those are children 2 and 3.

- `grep -rn 'preview.decide|preview.start|PREVIEW_COMMAND_MISSING|moe-preview-receipt' --include=*.ts apps/ packages/` = ZERO hits. Nothing to duplicate.
- The existing `apps/daemon/src/graph-preview-request.ts` and `apps/control-room/src/preview/` are PLAN/document previews, not the product preview. Do not extend them.

THE ROSTER, enumerated by tracing an existing human-only decide kind (`escalation.decide`) across the tree - these are the DAEMON-side files it touches, and the ones this row owns:
  apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-vocabulary.ts (kinds, capability, family table, PAYLOAD_KEYS, OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS)
  apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.ts and daemon-command-families.ts
  apps/daemon/src/daemon-v2-command-registry.ts
  apps/daemon/src/mcp-tool-allowlist.ts (EXCLUDED - operator only)
  packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts
  packages/control-room-client/src/generated/generated-client.ts and every digest mirror (memory generated-contract-digest-has-four-mirrors)

TWO HAZARDS MEASURED AT PLAN TIME, both of which have bitten this board before:
1. `HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS` IS DEFINED TWICE, byte-for-byte: apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawn-contract.ts:194 AND apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper.ts:116. Nothing found asserts the two agree. A new human-only kind added to only one of them leaves the wrapper free to staff an operator gate - exactly the class of defect that minted 8 junk goals live (see the comment at agent-wrapper.ts:117-123). Both must be updated and the row must add the assertion that they are equal.
2. Roster tests must be BIDIRECTIONAL set-equality (global rail 9): enumerate the SERVED set from the dispatch seam, not from the roster constant, or deleting an entry shrinks the iteration and stays green.
definitionOfDone: `preview.decide` is published across the full roster - vocabulary (kind, capability, family, PAYLOAD_KEYS, operator-principal), registry, families, v2 registry, contracts runtime vocabulary, generated client and every digest mirror. A bidirectional set-equality test enumerates the SERVED kinds from the dispatch seam and asserts they equal the advertised roster in BOTH directions (global rail 9); deleting the entry from either side must turn it red.

It is OPERATOR-ONLY and MCP-EXCLUDED: `preview.decide` appears in the MCP allowlist's exclusion set, and a test asserts an agent-authenticated dispatch is refused while an operator-authenticated one reaches the handler - asserting the refusal code and layer, not merely that it failed.

It is in BOTH HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS rosters (agent-spawn-contract.ts:194 and agent-wrapper.ts:116), AND a new test asserts the two sets are EQUAL to each other. That equality test is this row's most valuable artifact: the duplication exists today with nothing guarding it. Verify by deleting the entry from one roster only and confirming the test goes red.

The four refusal codes are defined with a closed code->layer map so a call site cannot mint a code and layer that disagree: PREVIEW_COMMAND_MISSING, PREVIEW_START_TIMEOUT, PREVIEW_GOAL_NOT_LANDED, PREVIEW_DECISION_INVALID. A test asserts each code's layer. Codes whose CONDITIONS belong to the runner (child 2) are defined here but may be exercised there - say so in the completion record rather than writing a fake condition to reach them.

The payload contract is exact-arity and refuses an unknown key rather than ignoring it: APPROVE carries no findings; REJECT carries findings naming the nodes to rework. A test asserts PREVIEW_DECISION_INVALID + layer for a malformed decision, for an unknown extra key, and for REJECT with empty findings.
Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test` (packages/contracts is touched, so the root lane is real evidence here).
taskRails: VOCABULARY ONLY. This row starts no process, captures no image, writes no receipt and renders no UI. If a step needs a running preview to be meaningful, it belongs to child 2 - say so and move on rather than stubbing a runner here.
HUMAN GATES ARE HUMAN-ONLY (inherited): operator-only, MCP-excluded, in BOTH HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS rosters, every refusal carrying a stable code asserted with its layer.
FEATURES ONLY (inherited): no security-boundary or policy work.

A new daemon command follows the 8-touchpoint + .js bridge pattern; a missing `.js` bridge kills the daemon at boot with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND (memory ui-connect-everything-built-2026-09-02). Never commit a generated index.js.

=== UNNAMED FILE 1: apps/daemon/src/daemon-store-dependencies.test.ts ===
A hard runtime red the moment `preview.decide` enters PAYLOAD_KEYS.
  :670  registryKinds: [...deps.registry.keys()].sort(),
  :745  registryKinds: [ ...46 kinds hand-written... ],
and the comment immediately above :745 reads verbatim: "The kind SET, not its size: a bare count lands every registration as an off-by-one naming nothing. A new command writes its own kind here."
The served set is DERIVED — daemon-command-registry.ts:392 is
  buildCommandRegistry((Object.keys(PAYLOAD_KEYS) as readonly WiredCommandKind[]).map(entryOf))
— so adding the PAYLOAD_KEYS entry adds the registry key, which reds this file. It is invisible to a grep for the command-kind literal in production source because it lives in a test table (the exact class global rail 19 names, and the same class of miss the plan's own risk section flags for the other two tables).

=== UNNAMED FILE 2: packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts ===
Explicitly moved OUT of this row by amend-1 ("Publishing it on the shared surface (MCP exclusion, packages/contracts, the regenerated client) ... moved to task-5f883e4e12c34842b3cb6c2f218e4256 ... Do not do that work here"), yet step 4 and step 5 cannot be done without it, for two independent reasons.

(i) TYPECHECK. RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS (:85-115) does not contain "preview.decide". Three declarations the plan's step 5 names are typed against the union derived from it:
  daemon-command-registry.test.ts:75   readonly kind: RuntimeCommandKind;      (the ROWS table at :91)
  daemon-command-registry.test.ts:280  const REGISTRATION_ORDER: readonly RuntimeCommandKind[]
  daemon-command-registry.test.ts:306  const OPERATOR_ONLY: readonly RuntimeCommandKind[]
and both sweeps are set-equality against the live registry, so a row cannot simply be omitted:
  :814  expect([...deps.registry.keys()].sort()).toEqual(ROWS.map((row) => row.kind).sort());
  :820  expect(REGISTRATION_ORDER).toHaveLength(46);
  :821  expect([...deps.registry.keys()]).toEqual(REGISTRATION_ORDER);
PROBE, written and deleted in the same command (`apps/daemon/src/zz-probe-worker56ac.ts`, contents `import type { RuntimeCommandKind } from "@moe/contracts"; export const PROBE: readonly RuntimeCommandKind[] = ["preview.decide"];`), run as `npx tsc --noEmit -p apps/daemon/tsconfig.json`, output verbatim:
  apps/daemon/src/zz-probe-worker56ac.ts(2,54): error TS2322: Type '"preview.decide"' is not assignable to type '"approval.decide" | "approval.decide_intent" | "blocker.challenge" | "blocker.open" | "blocker.resolve" | "budget.acknowledge_unknown_liability" | "budget.conservative_settle" | ... 95 more ... | "work.resume"'.
Probe removed; `ls` confirms absent. Full source is inline above so a grader can recreate it.
(NOTE: daemon-command-vocabulary.test.ts is NOT affected — its VocabularyRow.kind (:31) and OPERATOR_ONLY (:221) are typed WiredCommandKind, which is daemon-local and extensible from the new contract module. Only the registry test file is fenced by the shared union.)

(ii) REACHABILITY — the bigger one. DoD-2 requires "an operator-authenticated one reaches the handler" and step 4 requires "THE KIND MUST BE SERVED, NOT ONLY ADVERTISED". It cannot be, in this scope: apps/daemon/src/http/http-command-ingress.ts:152 calls decodeRuntimeCommandEnvelopeBytes, which at packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-envelope.ts:142 does `if (!isCommandKind(record["commandKind"])) return commandFailure(invalidInput());`, and isCommandKind (runtime-vocabulary.ts:134) tests membership in RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS. A preview.decide dispatch is therefore refused INPUT_INVALID at the envelope, BEFORE the registry and before the OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS fence. registry.test.ts's own `send` helper (:363) goes through handleCommandRequest, i.e. that same path — so even the test cannot reach the handler. Wiring the kind here without that line ships an advertised, registered, permanently unreachable command.

=== WHY I DID NOT JUST TAKE THE LINE ===
task-5f883e4e12c34842b3cb6c2f218e4256 is WORKING, order 31.5, and its DoD item 2 is verbatim "`preview.decide` is on the shared runtime command roster in packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts." Editing it here is the shared-worktree silent duplicate global rail 6 forbids, and it drags the four generated-contract digest mirrors that row's DoD item 3 owns. That row dependsOn THIS row, so I also cannot declare a dependency on it — that closes a cycle. This is an ordering/split defect only an architect can fix.

=== WHAT IS ALREADY DELIVERED AND GREEN (steps 2 and 3, DoD items 4 and 5) ===
apps/daemon/src/preview/preview-contracts.ts (249 lines) + .js bridge + preview-contracts.test.ts. `Test Files 1 passed (1)` / `Tests 30 passed (30)`, exit 0. Closed code->layer map, code roster derived from its keys, refusal factory with no layer argument, variant exact-arity decoder (APPROVE refuses a `findings` member as an unknown key; REJECT refuses an empty roster). Three mutation drills all RED and restored with SHA256 proof against out-of-tree backups (untracked files, so `git diff` is blind — global rail 13). Details in the step-2 and step-3 notes.

=== SMALLEST FIX I RECOMMEND ===
Amend this row to own ONE extra line in packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts (the RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS entry) plus apps/daemon/src/daemon-store-dependencies.test.ts, and strike DoD item 2 from task-5f883e4e (leaving it the MCP exclusion, the client regeneration + digest mirrors, HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS and the staffing test). That makes this row's delivered bytes actually reachable and keeps the digest-mirror work where it belongs. The alternative — re-splitting so a tiny leaf row lands the shared-roster line first — costs a round trip and this row would still have to wait on it.
